Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) so we can get a pilot scheduled. I put the SLOs below the bullet list and attached a lightweight checklist you can iterate on.

What we saw today
- Redwood demoed streaming + prefix caching for user message flows (~20–60 tokens typical).
- You confirmed 512-token summaries and up to ~2,000-token responses for some workflows.
- NimbleHealth priority is low-latency triage (chat-style) and batch scoring for nightly ingest.

Proposed performance SLOs (first pass)
- Chat (interactive streaming): p95 <= 150 ms for 128-token responses; streaming partials every 50–100ms.
- Summaries (512 tokens): p95 <= 300 ms for tail-preserving configs when streamed; or p95 <= 1200 ms for non-streamed large outputs.
- Batch scoring: sustained throughput target 2,000 tokens/sec (aggregate across workers), concurrency ~200 active requests.

MAP (next steps & owners)
1) Fill SLO checklist and return (attachment: nimble_slo_checklist.xlsx) — Samir (by 2027-03-05).
2) Redwood to propose pilot config and cost estimate (model variant, quantization, burst plan) — Marcus (by 2027-03-04).
3) Pilot kickoff call to lock infra and test dataset, 60m — schedule by Tessa (propose Wed/Thu next week).
4) Pilot agreement (1 month, limited dataset) — Priyom to share draft.

Attachments: nimble_slo_checklist.xlsx (SLO template), demo_recording_20270302.mp4 (recording), pilot_agreement_draft.pdf (placeholder).

If these SLOs miss the mark on your side, highlight the rows in the checklist and we’ll iterate. Can you confirm who will own the test dataset and point me to the sample payloads?

Tessa — thanks for the crisp summary. A few clarifying questions so we can sign off internally before the checklist update.

1) Streaming vs batching: for the chat flows we want partial token streaming (client shows incremental tokens). You list "streaming partials every 50–100ms" — is that an achievable guarantee or a best-effort? Our UX team wants to understand whether p95 streaming partial latency is a contractual SLO or an operational target.

2) For the 512-token summaries we are targeting p95 ~ 200–250 ms ideally — is that realistic on a single model variant, or does that require a separate low-latency quantized variant?

3) Concurrency definitions: when you say concurrency ~200 active requests, do you mean 200 concurrent open connections (websocket/stream) or 200 concurrent inference tokens-in-flight? We need the precise definitions for capacity planning.

4) Cost estimate: can Marcus or Priyom give a rough monthly cost estimate for a 1-month pilot configured to the proposed SLOs (assume 100k interactive requests, 200k summary runs, and nightly batch of 10M tokens)?

We own the sample payloads — I’ll drop a shared S3 link to anonymized payloads by EOD tomorrow.

Samir —

Quick technical replies to your numbered questions below. I’ll also attach a pre-filled SLO checklist we used internally (see nimble_slo_checklist.xlsx).

1) Streaming vs best-effort: Redwood’s streaming pipeline exposes server-sent-events/websocket-style chunking. We can make partials emitted at least every 100ms for the vast majority of steady-state sequences — that’s operationally realistic and we can treat it as a pilot-level SLO (p95 partial emission <= 150ms) with a fallback clause for cold KV cache misses. The main caveat is long-tail decoder steps when the model itself stalls (rare).

2) 512-token p95 at 200–250ms: that target is aggressive on general-purpose LLMs. Options to hit that range:
- Use a low-latency, aggressively quantized variant (8-bit or nf4) with shorter context kernels — likely achievable in p95 ~ 200–300ms depending on hardware.
- Split generation into streaming chunks (start sending partials early) which improves perceived latency even if total wall-clock is higher.

3) Concurrency definition: we define concurrency as "active in-flight requests" (open streams or outstanding HTTP calls that expect tokens). It maps roughly to concurrent sockets for interactive flows. For capacity planning we also normalize to tokens-in-flight; we’ll provide conversion guidance (example: 200 concurrent streams × avg 128 tokens/session ≈ X tokens/s based on per-token generation time).

4) Cost estimate (very rough, pilot config):
- Config: 2 x dedicated GPU nodes (A100-equivalent), autoscale to 4 for burst, optimized kv/prefix caching.
- Monthly pilot (1 month): $18–26k depending on model quantization and reserved-burst configuration. I’ll produce a more granular breakdown (token cost, node hours) in the next-day estimate.

Attached: nimble_slo_checklist.xlsx (pre-filled with suggested pilot SLOs). Also linking an internal note with streaming/batching tradeoffs: https://redwood-internal.company/docs/pilot-configs/nimblehealth-streaming-guide

Let me know if you want a short call with infra to walk through the conversion math.

—Marcus
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
